Remember, whether using an analog meter or a digital meter using the diode test function, current should flow in one direction only between the gate and the drain and the gate and the source.........
Reverse the leads, reverse biasing the gate to drain PN junction. A normal reading is high resistance. Low resistance reading indicates a shorted FET.
Second, measure the resistance of the gate to drain PN junction when forward biased. A low resistance reading is normal. A high resistance indicates an open FET.
Now reverse the test leads, reverse biasing the gate to source PN junction. The normal resistance measurement is high. A low reading indicates a shorted FET.
The normal resistance reading is low. A high reading indicates an open FET.
Remember, on some multimeters, the black lead is connected to the positive voltage source of the meter (Nida Model 480).
P CHANNEL FET - If checking a P channel FET, connect the negative potential lead to the gate and positive potential lead to the source.
N CHANNEL FET - The source and drain are made from the same type of semiconductor material, N. The gate is P type semiconductor material.
